assessment: The observations support investigating selection and layout interpretation together; they do not establish a common cause. Width overlap does not establish the cause of insertion retries. One hybrid is proposed as an unvalidated hypothesis.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an order-specific removable kit sheet could serve first as a component shadow board and then as a customer placement guide. Workers place each required partition on its outline, verify count and exterior color, and pack the checked kit with the sheet. Matching temporary labels connect each outline to its destination in the ordered layout, including the short partition.
openings.delta: Adapt the relationship between tools and empty silhouettes on a tool shadow board. Failed correspondence: an organizer partition has both a packed position and an installed position, which a simple silhouette cannot equate. Change the material assumptions from a fixed reusable board to a proposed removable sheet and from workshop assembly to checked customer assembly. Cross silhouette-based inventory checking with spatial assembly guidance at the shared partition-to-slot label interface: the same checked identity survives packing and becomes a placement instruction. Neither parent alone checks both presence and intended placement.
openings.prediction: The shared mapping should reduce short-partition placement errors beyond silhouettes alone and reduce kit omissions beyond layout guidance alone. Total workshop time may fall if avoided assembly exceeds sheet preparation and checking time.
openings.probe: Use spare board for sample kits, preserving all selected counts, colors, footprint and assortment. Compare checking-only, guidance-only, combined and current workflows, recording selection, preparation, checking, insertion and packing separately. Counterbalance worker order. Give ten participants fresh kits with combined or existing guidance; record unaided placement and short-partition errors. Treat this small comparison as exploratory. Before adoption, cost sheets and labels against 500 initial and 0.40 recurring limits, include setup in delivery capacity, and test all 60 pilot orders against the stated success measures.
assumptions: Provenance: the incumbent explicitly uses an order slip and base slots; verify the slip contains enough layout information before repurposing it into a partition-to-slot mapping.
Affordable sheet production, removable labels and sufficient preparation time are enabling dependencies, not supplied resources.
Customers can assemble checked kits unaided; this remains unproven. The guide is removed before use and makes no permanent bonds.
